_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::input_format#18 — CORRECTION fixture from the 2026-08-03 adversarial re-audit. The original pitfall text told the reader to capture 4C 'through a line-buffered pipe (stdbuf -oL -eL 4C in.4C.yaml out) or to a file'. The 'or to a file' half is FALSE and actively harmful: stdout to a regular file is fully buffered, so MPI_Abort discards the RESULT DESCRIPTION verdict exactly as it does for a pipe, and an agent that follows the advice sees a failed verification as an unexplained crash. Re-measured on 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf): 'BIN in out > f.log 2>&1' produced grep -c 'is WRONG' = 0 on three consecutive runs of a deliberately failing deck, while 'stdbuf -oL -eL BIN in out > f.log 2>&1' produced both the 'is WRONG' line and the 'Result check failed with 1 errors out of 1 tests' line. The fixture asserts the zero explicitly (IS_WRONG_LINES_IN_3_RUNS=0) so a future build that changes libc buffering, or an edit that reinstates the file advice, both show up. MUTATION CONTROL (T2_MUTATE=1, re-runnable): the plain-file-redirect arm is run under stdbuf -oL -eL. 'plain_file_redirect: IS_WRONG_LINES_IN_3_RUNS=0' disappears because the count becomes 3. Proved KILLED 2026-08-07. LOAD SENSITIVITY, observed 2026-08-07: this fixture asserts a COUNT OF ZERO 'is WRONG' lines across three unbuffered runs, so anything that lets stdout flush before MPI_Abort turns it red. On a 32-core host at load 30 one sweep reported VACUOUS_BASELINE (the unmutated staged copy did not pass) and an immediate re-run at the same commit reported KILLED. Treat a lone red here as a scheduling artefact until it reproduces on an idle machine; that is also why the arm repeats three times rather than once.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: arm (b) gets the very line buffering whose absence it exists to demonstrate. The 'is WRONG' line then survives the MPI_Abort in all three runs, IS_WRONG_LINES_IN_3_RUNS becomes 3, and the fixture must go red.
